description: TUM2TWIN provides terrestrial laser scans of the downtown TUM campus acquired on 5 April 2024 with a Leica P50 long-range scanner. The collection covers the Arcisstraße outdoor area and an indoor loop. Native documentation links subsampled point clouds, full-resolution observations and a complete collection with metadata. These access variants describe the same campaign and are grouped into one resource. They provide measured building and street geometry for the campus digital twin in Munich, Germany. The public description is freely accessible and links institutional storage. File access conditions, a dataset-specific licence and exact point spacing were not established from the descriptive page. Caveats include a documented 0.7551-metre offset in the Z direction needed for alignment with other TUM2TWIN components; the provider anticipates a future correction. This limitation must be checked before combining geometry. The record relates to the existing aggregate benchmark and remains distinct from the Ottobrunn laser scans. No storage listing, point cloud or viewer was opened.
